Here tabbat is an invocation (curse) and the second tabb means that he was destroyed, ruined, and his line was cut off. It is a report of the occurrence of the curse. In this brief verse, at the very beginning of the surah, there is a complete picture of the curse and its fulfilment. As it were, the contest comes to an end and the curtain falls.

The second verse that follows states the reality of the event.

﴿His wealth did not avail him, nor what he earned﴾ (2:111). His hands were broken; he was destroyed and ruined. His wealth and his struggle against Islam did not avail him, and neither his riches nor his cunning could save him from destruction. This was his end in the world. What will be his end in the Hereafter?

﴿He will be made to enter a Fire of blazing flame﴾ (3:111). Lahab (flame) indicates that this Fire will be very intense, blazing, and fiercely kindled.

﴿And his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾ (4:111). She too will be cast into that Fire, carrying bundles of firewood and in that state.

﴿Around her neck will be a rope of palm fiber﴾ (5:111). She will be bound in the Fire with that rope, or the rope is that with which firewood is bound. If its literal meaning is taken, she will go to Hell carrying a bundle of firewood and thorns; and if its figurative meaning is taken, the meaning is that she kindles the fire of mischief and strives to ignite the flames of sedition and strife.

The style of this surah is in harmony with its themes and meanings. An expression suited to the atmosphere of the surah has been adopted. In this connection, it is necessary to quote a few lines from my book "Scenes of the Resurrection in the Qur'an." Their quotation here is necessary because the revelation of this surah struck an arrow into the heart of Umm Jamil, due to which she became enraged and was left as if mad.

"Abu Lahab (father of flames) will be heated in a Fire that blazes, and his wife, who used to bring thorny bushes and place them on the path of the Messenger (ﷺ), will be thrown into Hell in a state where a rope of palm fiber is tied around her neck."

"The words are also proportionate and harmonious in sound, the images also consistent and uniform: she will be cast into Hell, which is blazing. In it the father of flames (Abu Lahab) will be cast. His wife brings firewood and places it in the path of Muhammad (ﷺ) and gives him harm, whether the literal or the metaphorical meaning is taken. Fire is kindled with firewood, and such firewood is brought bound with ropes. Therefore, in blazing Hell she will be bound with a rope of palm fiber, and she will be bound with the same rope with which she used to bring firewood, so that the punishment be like her crime. And this picture comes forward with its simple colours, and in its colour are firewood, rope, fire and flames. And in that Fire both husband and wife are being roasted."

From another angle too there is harmony in this surah. The sonic resonance of the words, the sound of binding a bundle of firewood, and the sound of tying a rope around the neck are also alike. Just recite:

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he!﴾ (1:111) The sonic harshness of the sound of shadd in these words is just like the tightness in binding a bundle of firewood. Just as these words are intense, so too the act of tying a rope around the neck and pulling it is intense. Throughout the whole surah there is this same atmosphere of constriction.

Thus there is a deep correspondence and harmony between the sound of the melody, the sound of the practical struggle, and the details of the movements of the surah. Then the words are of a kindred nature, and uniformity of expression is observed; all of these are in harmony with the atmosphere of the surah. Furthermore, all these things are also connected with the occasion of revelation and the background of the surah. All these artistic excellences are observed in just five short sentences, and in one of the shortest surahs of the Qur'an this artistic perfection has been displayed.

Because of these artistic excellences of the surah, and its overwhelming impact, the impression of Umm Jamil was that the Messenger (ﷺ) had satirized her. This surah spread immediately throughout Makkah, in which the husband and wife were condemned, threatened, and a very crude picture was drawn of them. It was a portrayal that shattered the heart of a self-conceited woman, who took great pride in her lineage and nobility and considered herself a woman of a very high household. But the Qur'an depicted her thus:

﴿The wife, the carrier of firewood, with a rope of fiber around her neck﴾ (4-5:111). This is a very common situation that was familiar among the Arabs.

Ibn Ishaq says: It has reached me that Umm Jamil, the carrier of firewood, when she heard about the revelation of this surah, that it was revealed about her and her husband, came out, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting near the Ka'bah, with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (ra) sitting with him. She had a fist full of stones. When she came and stood before the two of them, Allah veiled her eyes so that she could see only Abu Bakr. She said: "Where is your companion, Abu Bakr? I have been informed that he has satirized me. By Allah, if I found him, I would strike him with these stones. By Allah, I too am a poetess." Then she recited this couplet:

"We have disobeyed the reprehensible one (Muhammad),
and we have rejected his command and his religion."

She returned. Abu Bakr (ra) said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Did she not see you? He said: "She did not see me; Allah took her sight away from me."

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar narrated with his chain from Ibn Abbas (ra), when the surah "Tabbat yada..." (1:111) was revealed, the wife of Abu Lahab came into the sacred precinct while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr (ra) were sitting near the Ka'bah. Abu Bakr (ra) said: "O Messenger, if you move aside, she will not be able to harm you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A screen will come between me and her." She came and stood by Abu Bakr (ra) and said: "Abu Bakr, your companion has satirized us." Abu Bakr (ra) said: "By the Lord of this House, he has not done so; he neither composes poetry nor recites it." She said: "You are truthful." When she returned, Abu Bakr (ra) said: "O Messenger, did she not see you?" He said: "As long as she stood, the angels spread their wings over me until she left."

In short, her anger rose so high because this surah had spread, and she took it as satire. At that time satire was only in verse. Therefore Abu Bakr (ra) lawfully refuted the satire. And he was regarded as very truthful. But the contemptuous portrayal of her in these verses has been recorded in this everlasting Book. The Book of Allah is also imperishable, and the condemnation of both of them has become imperishable too. Indeed, this is a picture that speaks. This is the punishment for plotting against the Messenger (ﷺ) and his call. The truth is that whoever plots of this kind against the Islamic call and its proponents, failure is written in their destiny even in this world. They will be destroyed and ruined here, and in the Hereafter too they will receive a severe punishment. This is their fitting recompense. In the world, the woodcutter's rope, which points to humiliation, will in the Hereafter also be around her neck, and it will be a sufficient sign of disgrace.
